claims.source_title: The Role of Optical Frequency Comb Generators in AI Data Centers
claims.supporting_quote: Optical frequency combs generate many wavelengths from a single laser instead of using separate lasers per channel, cutting power, cost, and failure points as AI data centers scale to 16+ wavelengths per fiber.

claims.claim: Girardi said four wavelengths is a solved problem, difficulty starts at eight, and by 16 component count limits laser arrays.
claims.episode_span: four wavelengths is a solved problem
claims.source_title: The Role of Optical Frequency Comb Generators in AI Data Centers
claims.supporting_quote: “Four wavelengths is a solved problem, and arrays solve it well,” Girardi said. “The difficulty starts at eight, and by 16, the component count limits you.”

claims.claim: Girardi said one pump laser and one silicon nitride die produce all the wavelengths at once.
claims.episode_span: one pump laser and one silicon nitride die produce all the wavelengths at once
claims.source_title: The Role of Optical Frequency Comb Generators in AI Data Centers
claims.supporting_quote: One pump laser and one silicon nitride die produce all the wavelengths at once, on a grid set by the resonator itself, so the hardware does not grow as you add channels

claims.episode_span: pack many more wavelengths much tighter together without fear of interference.
claims.source_title: The Role of Optical Frequency Comb Generators in AI Data Centers
claims.supporting_quote: “Potentially, comb lasers allow you to pack many more wavelengths, much tighter together without fear of interference,” said Frank Smyth, founder and CTO of Pilot Photonics
